nodes.name: Scan Upcoming Events & Build Redis Plan

parameters.content:
## Frequency / scan window
Default schedule is every minute. Change the cron expression on **Schedule - Every Minute** if desired. The scanner fetches a bounded two-local-day horizon (today + tomorrow in `TIMEZONE`). Reminder/event keys are only materialized for future starts. The extra day supports the 21:00 next-day digest and reminders for meetings shortly after midnight.

## Redis scheduling contract
Reminder buckets: `calendar-notifier:reminders:v1:<offset>:<UTC-minute>:<calendarId>`
Day snapshots: `calendar-notifier:events:day:v1:<YYYY-MM-DD>:<calendarId>`
Reminder sent markers: `calendar-notifier:sent:v1:reminder:<offset>:<UTC-minute>:<eventKey>`
Change sent markers: `calendar-notifier:sent:v1:change:<messageId>`
Digest sent marker: `calendar-notifier:sent:v1:digest:<YYYY-MM-DD>`

Reminder sent markers prevent duplicate delivery when the every-minute workflow retries or overlaps.

## Failure safety
The calendar source registry `calendar-notifier:calendar-sources:v1` is persistent and is refreshed by the discovery workflow.

If the source registry is missing entirely (for example after a Redis flush or before discovery has run once), this workflow returns `skipped_source_registry_missing`, writes only a 5-minute health key, and performs **no deletes and no change/deletion detection**. Run/activate the discovery workflow to repopulate the registry.

If a calendar is still present in the discovery registry but its CalDAV/ICS fetch fails, the workflow marks it `stale_preserved` and keeps that calendar's previous Redis keys/snapshots untouched. **No deletion/change message is generated from a failed fetch.**

A successful fetch is authoritative. Missing future occurrences can generate `event_deleted`; changed title/time/location/meeting-link fields can generate `event_changed`. Naturally elapsed events do not generate deletion messages.

The first v2+ scan over an older v1 state establishes the comparison baseline without emitting change messages.

nodes.name: Build Delivery Candidates & Reminder Marker Reads

parameters.content:
## ntfy delivery + idempotency
The scanner also acts as the sender. It reads due reminder-minute buckets, checks permanent sent markers, then acquires a short **atomic Redis INCR claim** before publishing. This prevents overlapping executions from both sending the same notification. Successful sends get a 14-day sent marker; failed sends release their claim for retry. Claims expire after 120 seconds as a crash-recovery safety net.

At/after 21:00 in `TIMEZONE`, tomorrow's per-calendar day snapshots are combined into one digest and guarded by `calendar-notifier:sent:v1:digest:<YYYY-MM-DD>`. Meeting URLs are included in the body and as ntfy `click` targets when present.
